item.title: [Recap] Stephon Castle (SAS): Stephon Castle led the Spurs with 26 points (10-of-15 FGs), four rebounds, nine assists, two steals, one block, four three-pointers and six turnovers in a 99-96 win over the Lakers on Friday.
item.description:
Stephon Castle led the Spurs with 26 points (10-of-15 FGs), four rebounds, nine assists, two steals, one block, four three-pointers and six turnovers in a 99-96 win over the Lakers on Friday.

Even with De’Aaron Fox and Dylan Harper back, Castle was still able to have a strong night. He led the team in scoring and nearly recorded a double-double while still posting a full stat line. It was a slow start to the year for Castle, but he has really picked things up as of late. Over his last eight games, Castle has averaged 22.0 points, 4.8 rebounds, 8.6 assists and 1.3 steals per game, though the most impressive part may be that he has made 3.0 triples per game while shooting 50 percent from deep during that stretch. Castle has had his limitations, and they’re still evident at times (six turnovers), but he is clearly capable of making a big impact for the Spurs and stuffing the stat sheet for fantasy managers. The shooting development is critical to his future, as he has gone from poor shooting prospect to a legitimate threat from deep in just a couple of seasons.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Brandon Ingram (LAC): Brandon Ingram got himself 15 points (6-of-15 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, and three steals in the loss to the Pelicans on Friday.
item.description:
Brandon Ingram got himself 15 points (6-of-15 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, and three steals in the loss to the Pelicans on Friday.

It’s been a rough start for Ingram since he’s shooting 34.6% from the field, and 12.5% from three in his three games back from his Achilles injury. He’s still giving you decent counting stats despite the bad efficiency. He should be rostered in redraft leagues and could be seen as a buy low candidate. He should not continue to shoot with this efficiency and will get more comfortable with the Clippers. There could be a shut down risk considering the Clippers don’t have access to their first round pick.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Brook Lopez (LAC): Brook Lopez put up 17 points (4-of-11 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), six rebounds, an assist, a block, and two 3-pointers in the loss to the Pelicans on Friday.
item.description:
Brook Lopez put up 17 points (4-of-11 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), six rebounds, an assist, a block, and two 3-pointers in the loss to the Pelicans on Friday.

Brook Lopez was a +16 a game where they lost by 1 which shows how impactful he was on the game. He’s not the same Brook Lopez of old, especially as his speed and athleticism have diminished. However, he’s smart enough to where he’s able to continue to be on the floor and be a useful player. For most redraft leagues, he should probably be on a roster even though the upside isn’t high. He’s averaging 14.6 points and 5.1 rebounds on the season.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Darius Garland (LAC): Darius Garland got 19 points (7-of-15 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, nine assists, a steal, three 3-pointers, and eight turnovers in the 105-104 loss to the Pelicans on Friday.
item.description:
Darius Garland got 19 points (7-of-15 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, nine assists, a steal, three 3-pointers, and eight turnovers in the 105-104 loss to the Pelicans on Friday.

The eight turnovers really hurt as it likely cost the Clippers the game in the end. On the season, Garland has been pretty good in the counting stats if you are punting turnovers. Now that he’s the primary scoring option, his turnovers have jumped to 4.2 per game when his previous high was 3.6 in the 21-22 season. If he’s healthy, he will continue to produce like he has.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] De'Aaron Fox (SAS): De’Aaron Fox returned to the lineup on Friday and finished with 12 points (5-of-10 FGs), five rebounds and two assists against the Lakers.
item.description:
De’Aaron Fox returned to the lineup on Friday and finished with 12 points (5-of-10 FGs), five rebounds and two assists against the Lakers.

Fox was back in the lineup following a two-game absence, but he continued to provide limited value despite immediately starting and playing just under 30 minutes. Still, the Spurs were able to get the win. Fox started the year off fine, but his production has dropped over the last few weeks. Hopefully that will improve moving forward, but right now, things are rough, making it difficult to rely on Fox.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Dylan Harper (SAS): Dylan Harper returned to the lineup on Friday and finished with 14 points (6-of-11 FGs), four rebounds and three assists against the Lakers.
item.description:
Dylan Harper returned to the lineup on Friday and finished with 14 points (6-of-11 FGs), four rebounds and three assists against the Lakers.

The initial diagnosis for Harper was that he would miss 1-3 weeks, and he only ended up being sidelined for four games. He was on a minutes restriction for his first game back, and he came off the bench, which limited his statistical output. However, he was still really impactful during his time on the floor. He only played 24 minutes in this game, but that role should expand as he logs more games, and he’ll eventually push Julian Champagnie back to the bench.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Walker Kessler (LAL): Walker Kessler recorded a double-double on Friday with 10 points (3-of-5 FGs), 13 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block against the Spurs.
item.description:
Walker Kessler recorded a double-double on Friday with 10 points (3-of-5 FGs), 13 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block against the Spurs.

In a tough matchup against Victor Wembanyama, Kessler was able to record a double-double for the eighth time in his last nine games. Kessler continues to dominate in traditional big man stats, though he also matched his season high for assists in this one. Kessler will continue to put up plenty of rebounds and blocks while maintaining a strong field goal percentage, but he won’t pop in other categories often.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Jordan Poole (NOP): Jordan Poole put up 16 points (4-of-10 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, a steal, and three 3-pointers in the win over the Clippers on Friday.
item.description:
Jordan Poole put up 16 points (4-of-10 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, a steal, and three 3-pointers in the win over the Clippers on Friday.

After a really bad start, Jordan Poole has gotten better with his scoring and has had a really good month. He can be useful in some leagues if you need his scoring and 3PT shooting, but his upside is limited given his role on the team. There is a sell high open here in deeper leagues since his efficiency is higher than what he’s done on average over his career, but he has been getting to the line and the rim more.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Immanuel Quickley (TOR): Immanuel Quickley recorded a triple-double on Friday with 24 points (8-of-15 FGs), 10 rebounds, 14 assists, one steal and four three-pointers in a 124-100 win over the Nets.
item.description:
Immanuel Quickley recorded a triple-double on Friday with 24 points (8-of-15 FGs), 10 rebounds, 14 assists, one steal and four three-pointers in a 124-100 win over the Nets.

For the third time in his career and the first time since his second season, Quickley recorded a triple-double. He also set a season high for assists in what was his best performance of the season. Quickley has had a solid season, but this type of production isn’t something managers should expect to come often. Quickly has seen his usage increase with all the injuries they’re facing, which is a trend that should continue with Kawhi Leonard (knee) and RJ Barrett (hamstring) still sidelined.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Scottie Barnes (TOR): Scottie Barnes led the Raptors with 34 points (11-of-20 FGs, 10-of-10 FTs), one rebound, five assists, three blocks and two three-pointers against the Nets on Friday.
item.description:
Scottie Barnes led the Raptors with 34 points (11-of-20 FGs, 10-of-10 FTs), one rebound, five assists, three blocks and two three-pointers against the Nets on Friday.

Barnes got off to a hot start in this game, scoring 22 points in the first half alone. He didn’t stay quite as hot after the break, but he was still able to turn in another strong scoring night. He has scored at least 30 points in three of his last five games while averaging 28.8 points, 4.8 rebounds, 4.8 assists, 2.2 blocks and 1.8 triples per game during this stretch. He’ll look to keep it going against the Nuggets on Sunday to close out the week.

Noah Rubin

item.description:

item.title: [Recap] Cam Spencer (MEM): Cam Spencer put up 16 points (7-of-14 FGs), six rebounds, four assists, three steals, two blocks, and two 3-pointers in the win over the Timberwolves on Wednesday.
item.description:
Cam Spencer put up 16 points (7-of-14 FGs), six rebounds, four assists, three steals, two blocks, and two 3-pointers in the win over the Timberwolves on Wednesday.

Cam Spencer excels in his role as a bench scorer and being one of the best shooters in the NBA. Despite the lackluster athleticism, his ability to decelerate and take smart shots is why he’s still in the NBA. He attacks the glass, he can pass, he can defend, and he’s a psychopath competitor. He’s a streamer in redraft leagues, and in deeper dynasty leagues, he should be a good player despite him being older for being a newer player in the NBA.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Damian Lillard (POR): Damian Lillard had a monster 29 points (7-of-20 FGs, 10-of-10 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, two steals, and five 3-pointers in the win over the Spurs on Wednesday.
item.description:
Damian Lillard had a monster 29 points (7-of-20 FGs, 10-of-10 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, two steals, and five 3-pointers in the win over the Spurs on Wednesday.

He had a couple down games, so it’s good to see him bounce back. Damian Lillard continues to show up in big moments and was good in this one. He gave you a real boost from the free throw line and a good bump in points. On the season, he hasn’t been as efficient from the field compared to previous seasons, but considering his age and injury history, it might be part of the deal with Lillard at this point in his career.

item.description:
Sidy Cissoko got himself 16 points (6-of-14 FGs), four rebounds, two assists, two steals, a block, and four 3-pointers against the Spurs on Wednesday.

While the stats don’t exactly show it, he’s been good for Portland this season and has been great at balancing out the lineup with Ja Morant injured. He’s had good outings from a fantasy perspective in three of the past four games. He’s more of a streamer but in deeper leagues given that he doesn’t put up a lot of numbers when he’s on the court. In dynasty leagues, he’s a solid deeper league option who could provide sneaky value.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Deni Avdija (POR): Deni Avdija put up 33 points (11-of-21 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), 12 rebounds, seven assists, two steals, and five 3-pointers in the 111-116 win over the Spurs on Wednesday.
item.description:
Deni Avdija put up 33 points (11-of-21 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), 12 rebounds, seven assists, two steals, and five 3-pointers in the 111-116 win over the Spurs on Wednesday.

Avdija’s rim pressure was on full display which was a big reason why the Blazers were as competitive as they were. That should improve, but he has had seasons shooting in the 70’s from the free throw line.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Devin Vassell (SAS): Devin Vassell had 18 points (6-of-18 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, an assist, two steals, a block, and three 3-pointers in the loss to the Blazers on Wednesday.
item.description:

He even filled up the box score with the peripheral stats that you don’t often get from him. While Fox is out, Vassell should be receive a bump in scoring.

item.description:

item.title: [Recap] Victor Wembanyama (SAS): Victor Wembanyama had 44 points (17-of-30 FGs, 7-of-10 FTs), 16 rebounds, three assists, a steal, two blocks, and three 3-pointers in the 111-116 loss to the Blazers on Wednesday.
item.description:
Victor Wembanyama had 44 points (17-of-30 FGs, 7-of-10 FTs), 16 rebounds, three assists, a steal, two blocks, and three 3-pointers in the 111-116 loss to the Blazers on Wednesday.

item.title: [Recap] Emanuel Sharp (SAC): Emanuel Sharp finished Wednesday’s loss to the Warriors with nine points (3-of-6 FGs), two rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers.
item.description:
Emanuel Sharp finished Wednesday’s loss to the Warriors with nine points (3-of-6 FGs), two rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers.

Zach LaVine was not available for Wednesday’s game due to a knee injury. Instead of Malik Monk (five points, four assists and one steal), Kings head coach Doug Christie prioritized defense and started Sharp. The rookie shot the ball well, making three of his six attempts. However, Sharp’s struggles to defend without fouling landed him in foul trouble, and he eventually fouled out in the fourth quarter. If LaVine remains out, Sharp could get more starts, as a low-usage guard who seems to fit well alongside Darius Acuff Jr.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Keegan Murray (SAC): Keegan Murray recorded 18 points (8-of-19 FGs), four rebounds, two assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Warriors.
item.description:
Keegan Murray recorded 18 points (8-of-19 FGs), four rebounds, two assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Warriors.

Murray appears to be making strides offensively after a slow start to the season, as he extended his streak of games with double-digit scoring to five. The 18 points were a season high for the Kings forward, who is shooting 49.2 percent from the field over the last five games. Murray’s free-throw percentage during this stretch (50.0) is low, but he’s attempted four foul shots total, making two. His season-long fantasy value remains low, but things may be looking up for managers who refused to throw in the towel.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Darius Acuff (SAC): Darius Acuff Jr. accounted for 22 points (9-of-24 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, nine assists and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Warriors.
item.description:

Acuff’s efficiency took a hit on Wednesday, as he needed 24 shots to score 22 points and committed five turnovers. However, given some of the stout individual defenders on the Warriors’ roster, this performance isn’t surprising. Even with the turnover concerns, Acuff has provided top-75 value in nine-cat formats. With the Kings all-in on the rookie guard, he’ll have every opportunity to maintain that production level, if not improve it.

item.title: [Recap] Brandin Podziemski (GSW): Brandin Podziemski recorded a team-high 18 points (5-of-14 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds and two assists over 37 minutes to lead the Warriors to an 88-87 win over the Celtics on Sunday.
item.description:
Brandin Podziemski recorded a team-high 18 points (5-of-14 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds and two assists over 37 minutes to lead the Warriors to an 88-87 win over the Celtics on Sunday.

Podziemski helped Golden State snap a five-game losing streak in a low-scoring slugfest where both teams shot below 40 percent from the floor and failed to reach 90 points. He knocked down a clutch three-pointer to put the Warriors ahead with just over two minutes left on the clock and they managed to hold off the Celtics the rest of the way. He’ll continue to play an increased role while Stephen Curry remains sidelined with a partially-torn oblique. The Warriors have a three-game week on tap that includes matchups against the Kings, Trail Blazers and Clippers.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Jayson Tatum (BOS): Jayson Tatum amassed 27 points (8-of-20 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), 10 rebounds, six assists and one steal over 38 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors.
item.description:
Jayson Tatum amassed 27 points (8-of-20 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), 10 rebounds, six assists and one steal over 38 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors.

Tatum scored 23 first-half points to pass Bill Russell for eighth place on the franchise’s all-time scoring list and keep Boston within striking distance. It wasn’t enough as he went ice-cold in the second half as the Celtics dropped their fourth straight game. He missed a critical free throw in the final minute before failing to nail a wide-open three-pointer that would’ve put the Celtics ahead in the final 30 seconds. He had a chance to deliver a game-winner following a huge steal by Hugo González, but missed a fadeaway over Draymond Green. The 28-year-old fantasy star has delivered second-round value this season, averaging 26.4 points, 6.9 rebounds, 6.7 assists, 0.7 steals and 0.7 blocks through 15 games. The Celtics have a three-game week coming up featuring showdowns against the Wizards, Hawks and Spurs.

George Bissell
